items.title: Types of Schemes & the DBT/JAM Delivery Backbone
items.body:
## Central Sector vs Centrally Sponsored

| Feature | Central Sector Scheme | Centrally Sponsored Scheme (CSS) |
|---|---|---|
| Funding | 100% by the Union | Shared Centre–State (e.g. 60:40, 90:10 for special-category) |
| Subject | Central List / national-scope | Largely State List subjects |
| Examples | PM-KISAN, PM Suryaghar | MGNREGA, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission, POSHAN |

## DBT & the JAM trinity

- **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** sends benefits straight to beneficiaries' bank accounts, cutting middlemen, ghost beneficiaries and delays.
- It rides on the **JAM trinity — Jan Dhan (accounts) + Aadhaar (ID) + Mobile (connectivity)**.
- Result: better targeting, fewer leakages, faster payouts across both central and AP state schemes.
keyPoints: Central Sector Schemes are 100% Union-funded (e.g. PM-KISAN); Centrally Sponsored Schemes share cost Centre–State (e.g. MGNREGA, PMAY, Jal Jeevan Mission).
DBT transfers benefits directly to bank accounts, reducing leakage and middlemen.
JAM trinity = Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile — the digital backbone of DBT.
Special-category/NE and hill states often get a more favourable CSS ratio (e.g. 90:10).
items.source: NITI Aayog / Union Budget / Economic Survey — scheme classification & DBT

items.title: Major Central Welfare Schemes — Quick Table
items.body:
## Flagship Central Schemes

| Scheme | Ministry / Domain | Core benefit |
|---|---|---|
| PM-KISAN | Agriculture | ₹6,000/yr income support (3 × ₹2,000) |
| Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY | Health (NHA) | ₹5 lakh/family health cover; 70+ universal (2024) |
| PMAY (Urban 2.0 / Gramin) | Housing | Pucca houses — 'Housing for All' |
| MGNREGA (2005) | Rural Dev | 100 days guaranteed wage employment |
| PM Ujjwala Yojana | Petroleum | Free LPG connections to poor women |
| Jal Jeevan Mission | Jal Shakti | 'Har Ghar Jal' tap connections |
| PMJDY | Finance | Zero-balance accounts, financial inclusion |
| PM SVANidhi / PM Vishwakarma | Urban / MSME | Micro-credit to vendors; artisan support |
| PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli | New & Renewable Energy | Rooftop solar, up to 300 free units |

## Health & human development

- **POSHAN Abhiyaan / POSHAN 2.0** — tackles malnutrition, stunting, anaemia.
- **NEP 2020** — 5+3+3+4 curricular structure, mother-tongue early learning.
keyPoints: PM-KISAN = ₹6,000/year in three installments (central sector).
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY = ₹5 lakh family health cover; extended to all 70+ in 2024.
MGNREGA (2005) legally guarantees 100 days of wage employment with social audit.
PM Ujjwala = free LPG to poor women; Jal Jeevan Mission = 'Har Ghar Jal' tap water.
PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) subsidises rooftop solar with up to 300 free units.
items.mnemonic: Central big-ticket: 'KISAN AAYUSHMAN AWAS NAREGA UJJWALA JAL' — income, health, house, work, gas, water.

items.title: AP Flagship — The 'Super Six' Guarantees (2024 TDP-NDA)
items.body:
## Context

- The **TDP-led NDA (TDP–Jana Sena–BJP)** government took office in Andhra Pradesh in **June 2024** under CM **N. Chandrababu Naidu**.
- Its six headline poll guarantees are branded the **'Super Six'**, rolled out in phases (2024–2026).

## The Six Guarantees

| # | Scheme | Core benefit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Thalliki Vandanam** | ~₹15,000/yr per child to mothers for schooling |
| 2 | **Annadata Sukhibhava** | ~₹20,000/yr to farmer families (incl. PM-KISAN) |
| 3 | **Deepam 2.0** | 3 free LPG cylinders per year to women |
| 4 | **Free bus travel** | Zero-fare travel for women in state (APSRTC) buses |
| 5 | **Adabidda Nidhi** | ~₹1,500/month to eligible women (19–59) |
| 6 | **Youth unemployment allowance** | ~₹3,000/month to unemployed youth |

> The earlier YSRCP government's package was branded **Navaratnalu** (Amma Vodi, Rythu Bharosa, etc.) — distinct from the Super Six.
keyPoints: AP 'Super Six' are the 2024 TDP-led NDA (TDP–JSP–BJP) government's flagship guarantees under CM Chandrababu Naidu.
Thalliki Vandanam ≈ ₹15,000/year per child schooling support to mothers.
Annadata Sukhibhava ≈ ₹20,000/year to farmer families, inclusive of central PM-KISAN.
Deepam 2.0 = 3 free LPG cylinders/year; free bus travel = zero-fare for women in state buses.
Adabidda Nidhi ≈ ₹1,500/month to women (19–59); youth get ≈ ₹3,000/month unemployment allowance.
The previous YSRCP package 'Navaratnalu' (Amma Vodi, Rythu Bharosa) is a separate, older set.
items.mnemonic: Super Six = 'Mother, Farmer, Gas, Bus, Woman-cash, Youth-cash'.
items.source: Government of Andhra Pradesh — Super Six scheme launches & TDP-NDA manifesto (2024)

items.title: Super Six — How They Interlock with Central Schemes
items.body:
## State top-ups on central schemes

- **Annadata Sukhibhava** is explicitly **structured to include the central PM-KISAN ₹6,000**, with the State adding a top-up to reach ~₹20,000 — avoiding duplication and stretching each rupee.
- **Deepam 2.0** complements the **central Ujjwala** connection scheme by funding **free refills**, so the connection (Centre) and the fills (State) work together.

## Delivery and design themes

- Most Super Six benefits are **DBT-based**, routed through Aadhaar-linked accounts (the JAM logic).
- The government also promotes a **'P4' (Public–Private–People Partnership)** model for poverty reduction, pairing better-off families/private actors with the poorest households.
- **Mega DSC** teacher recruitment and ration door-delivery were allied governance promises.
keyPoints: Annadata Sukhibhava is built on top of central PM-KISAN (₹6,000) with a state top-up to ~₹20,000.
Deepam 2.0 (free refills) complements the central Ujjwala connection scheme.
Super Six benefits are largely DBT-based via Aadhaar-linked accounts.
AP's 'P4' = Public–Private–People Partnership model for poverty reduction.
Allied promises included Mega DSC teacher recruitment and ration door-delivery.
items.source: Government of Andhra Pradesh — scheme GOs & P4 initiative

items.title: Newer Central Schemes for Livelihoods & Energy
items.body:
## Livelihood micro-support

- **PM SVANidhi** — collateral-free working-capital micro-loans to **street vendors**, with incentives for digital transactions.
- **PM Vishwakarma** (2023) — for **traditional artisans and craftspeople** (18 trades): skilling, a toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit.

## Energy & clean power

- **PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana** (2024) — subsidised **rooftop solar**, targeting **1 crore households** with up to **300 free units/month**.

## Housing update

- **PMAY-Urban 2.0** approved in 2024 to build additional urban houses; **PMAY-Gramin** extended with more rural houses sanctioned.
keyPoints: PM SVANidhi gives collateral-free micro-loans to street vendors; PM Vishwakarma (2023) supports 18 traditional artisan trades.
PM Suryaghar Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) targets 1 crore rooftop-solar homes, up to 300 free units/month.
PMAY-Urban 2.0 was approved in 2024; PMAY-Gramin extended with more sanctioned houses.
These newer schemes emphasise livelihoods, clean energy and the missing 'last-mile' groups.
items.source: PIB — PM SVANidhi, PM Vishwakarma, PM Suryaghar, PMAY 2.0

items.title: Implementation, Convergence & Accountability
items.body:
## Common implementation challenges

- **Exclusion & inclusion errors** in beneficiary lists; **leakages** and ghost beneficiaries (DBT mitigates these).
- **Thin last-mile capacity** (staff, digital access); **poor convergence** across overlapping schemes.
- **Fiscal strain** on states running large cash-transfer guarantees.

## Tools & reforms

- **Outcome budgeting** — measures results (outcomes), not just spending (outlays).
- **Social audit** — statutorily mandated under **MGNREGA**; Gram Sabha scrutiny of works.
- **DBT + JAM** — plug leakages and speed delivery.
- **2nd ARC** reports recommended citizen-centric administration, single-window delivery and grievance redressal (e.g. CPGRAMS).

## AP delivery layer

- AP uses **MeeSeva/ward-secretariat** style last-mile delivery and a **P4** partnership model for poverty reduction.
keyPoints: Key challenges: exclusion/inclusion errors, leakages, thin last-mile capacity, weak convergence, fiscal strain.
Outcome budgeting shifts focus from outlays to measurable outcomes.
Social audit is statutorily mandated under MGNREGA (Gram Sabha scrutiny).
2nd ARC pushed citizen-centric, single-window delivery and grievance redressal (CPGRAMS).
AP relies on ward/village secretariats and the P4 model for last-mile delivery.
items.source: 2nd ARC reports / NITI Aayog / MGNREGA social-audit framework

items.title: PYQ Precision — Scheme Numbers, Matching & YSR-era AP
items.body:
## Central-scheme facts (frequently tested)

| Scheme | Key number/fact |
|---|---|
| **PMFBY** (2016) | Farmer premium **2% Kharif / 1.5% Rabi / 5% commercial-hort** |
| **PMJJBY** (2015) | Life cover ₹2 lakh |
| **PMSBY** (2015) | Accident cover ₹2 lakh |
| **Atal Pension Yojana** | Guaranteed old-age pension (unorganised sector) |
| **Mission Indradhanush** | Full immunisation (children + pregnant women) |
| **SWAYAM** | Online MOOCs (Education Ministry) |
| **DDU-GKY** | Rural youth skilling & placement (MoRD) |
| **MPLADS** | Durable assets; unused funds **carried forward** (do not lapse) |

## YSR-era AP schemes (2019-24, 'Navaratnalu')

- **Amma Vodi** — ₹15,000/yr to mothers for schooling; **YSR Rythu Bharosa** — farmer income support (+PM-KISAN); **YSR Aarogyasri** — health cover; **YSR Cheyutha** — women 45-60; **Jagananna Vidya Deevena** — fee reimbursement.
- Distinct from the **2024 NDA 'Super Six'** (Thalliki Vandanam, Annadata Sukhibhava, Deepam-2, free bus travel, Adabidda Nidhi, youth allowance).
keyPoints: PMFBY farmer premium: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi, 5% commercial/horticultural crops.
PMJJBY = life cover, PMSBY = accident cover (each ₹2 lakh, 2015); Atal Pension Yojana = old-age pension.
Mission Indradhanush = immunisation; SWAYAM = MOOCs; DDU-GKY = rural skilling.
MPLADS funds build durable assets and can be carried forward (do not lapse).
YSR-era AP schemes: Amma Vodi (schooling), Rythu Bharosa (farmers), Aarogyasri (health) — distinct from the 2024 Super Six.
